narrative:
The model determined that you have an 84.8% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this predicted risk is so high, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors, ranked by importance. Your first-year and third-year class rankings had the strongest influence, both pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. You placed in the bottom decile for grades in both Year 1 and Year 3, far below the average of roughly the 6th decile among students who were accepted. These unusually low academic standings in law school were the main reasons the model saw you as unlikely to pass the bar.

Your LSAT score was the third most important factor, but it worked in the opposite direction. At 40, your score sits above the 37.2 average of accepted students, which gave the model some confidence you could succeed. Unfortunately, this positive signal was not strong enough to overcome the negative impact of your class rankings.

The model did not consider your gender or race in any way. Given these results, you should focus on improving your academic performance and consider retaking key courses or seeking additional academic support before reapplying. Strengthening your class standing would likely have the biggest effect on future predictions. (218 words)
